form: 1-3 Hebrew letters on sherd tags: ט, מ, קא, ת, שק, גב, גט, כי etc.
interpretation_given_by_source: ט = ṭevel (untithed); מ = maʿaser (tithe); קא = qorban/qodesh; ת = terumah; שק = "sack"; many others unexplained

form: Greek Α, Β or Θ beside a Palaeo-Hebrew letter; Α + Palaeo-Hebrew yod after the name יהוחנן (dozens of sherds)
interpretation_given_by_source: "alpha might be a mark for a select kind or quality of a specific product"; yod possibly יין (wine), "ten" or "tithe"

form: ΚΓ (Greek numeral 23) repeated in Phoenician-type numerals, with לג (log); others "21 log", "20 log"
interpretation_given_by_source: capacity of a jar in log, written once in Greek numerals
source: IIP masa0595 (Masada I no. 595), masa0593-0594; masa0924 κγ "is a numeral" (IIP cites Masada I no. 924; probably Masada II - unverified)

interpretation_given_by_source: σέ(α) seah, κά(βοι) qab, β(άτοι) bat, πυ(ρός) wheat, ἐρ(έβινθος) chickpea, φ(όρος) tax, ἀρ(γυρίου) silver, δ(ῶρον) gift

form: agoranomos legends with L + year numerals; single letter Η
interpretation_given_by_source: "H is possibly a weight mark, probably meaning 1/8, or the short form of ἡμι- (half)"
source: IIP mare0216 (Korzakova 2010, "Lead Weights", no. 9); mare0220 ἡμιόγδοον

site: Qumran caves, Kh. Qumran, Ein Feshkha
form: 21 Greek of 93 inscriptions: 6Q2 jar with single Greek μ; Fesh. 71 weight ΛΕΒ; KhQ 635 "log"; KhQ 192 "ta kol"
interpretation_given_by_source: μ = initial of a name or a measure (μέτρον/seah preferred by Hamidovic); ΛΕΒ = L(year) 5, and β(ασιλέως) or 2
source: Hamidovic 2009, ICOS 23 Proceedings pp. 466-468, citing Lemaire 2003 pp. 342, 358, 381 and de Vaux 1973 pp. 67-69

system: Greek letter groups on Jewish ossuaries
form: ΙΦΚΧ; ΧΨ ΑΒ; Κ·ΝΙΦ; ΘΗ (one letter in each metope)
interpretation_given_by_source: "initials of the deceased" (Tzaferis; IIP calls them "enigmatic"); ΘΗ "might be the initials"

site: Herodium (tholos cornice), Masada (~70 drums), Jericho early Herodian palace
form: single Hebrew (Jewish-script) letters, sometimes 2 letters, with diagonal bars as numerals (up to 8)
interpretation_given_by_source: assembly/position marks; letters in alphabetic order, bars = sequence
source: Eshel in Porat, Chachy & Kalman, Herodium I (2015) pp. 463-464, citing Foerster 1995 pp. 80, 98-99, Martin 1965, Salmon 1965

form: Hebrew letters (e.g. aleph) as lid direction marks
interpretation_given_by_source: fitting marks for lid and chest

site: Jerusalem Temple (as remembered in the Mishnah)
form: א ב ג on the three 3-seah baskets; R. Ishmael: written in Greek, alpha beta gamma
interpretation_given_by_source: order of filling / order of use of the funds (Davidson English gloss)

form: four seals inscribed עגל, זכר, גדי, חוטא (Ben Azzai: five, in Aramaic)
interpretation_given_by_source: receipts redeemable for libations; reconciled each evening

form: 13 shofar-chests labelled with the purpose of the funds (Aramaic תקלין חדתין, תקלין עתיקין ...)
